title: Kafka-style Message Queue: Complete Architecture
description: Design a log-based distributed queue with partitions, replication, consumer groups, and offsets.

data.text: Design a distributed message queue that supports high-throughput pub-sub, durable storage, horizontal scaling, and replay.

terms.definition: An append-only, ordered sequence of messages on disk.
A shard of a topic that allows parallel writes and reads.
A group of consumers that together process all partitions with at-least-once delivery.
A sequential index pointing to a message in a partition log.
Replicas that are fully caught up with the leader and can take over on failure.

data.caption: Kafka-style: Brokers manage partition leaders/followers, ZooKeeper/Controller for metadata, Producers, and Consumer Groups
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    Producers[Producers]
    Brokers[Brokers with Partition Leaders/Followers]
    Controller[Kafka Controller/Metadata]
    Consumers[Consumer Groups]
    Storage[Disk-backed Log Segments]

    Producers --> Brokers
    Brokers --> Storage
    Controller --> Brokers
    Brokers --> Consumers

items: Messages are written to the partition leader and replicated to followers
Consumers track their offset per partition (often in an internal topic)
Partitioning key determines which partition a message goes to
ISR ensures only caught-up replicas can become leader

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Log-based storage enables replay and high throughput via sequential I/O
Partitioning + consumer groups give horizontal scaling
Pull-based consumption gives consumers control over flow
data.takeaway: A Kafka-style queue is a distributed commit log: partition for scale, replicate for durability, pull for control.
